caption: Some months it's R18 000, some months it's R9 000, and this was one of the thin ones. Whose income never looks the same twice?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R13 800
p/m income
Living in Soweto
slides.body:
Female, 24
Single, renting a room from her aunt
Job: Hairdresser, rents a chair
Net income: R13 800 p/m (this month)

slides.title: Chair rental
slides.includes: Booth rent at the salon, paid whether I have clients or not
slides.body: It comes out first, before I know what the month even looks like.

slides.title: Room rent
slides.includes: One room in my aunt's house in Soweto, water and lights included
slides.body: Cheaper than my own place, and I still hand over half of it some weeks without blinking.

slides.title: Stock
slides.includes: Relaxer, weaves, colour, bought from my own pocket before I earn a cent back
slides.body: I over-bought last month and I'm still working through it. Bad month for stock, worse month for cash flow.

slides.title: Taxi fare
slides.includes: To the salon and to the wholesalers for stock runs
slides.body: No car yet. This is the one that surprises people most.

slides.title: Stokvel
slides.includes: Twelve of us, payout comes round every December
slides.body: Non-negotiable. I've missed rent before I've missed this.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Airtime & data, electricity, groceries, funeral policy, takeaways, product touch-ups between clients
slides.body: Six small things I never add up in one sitting. Together they're almost a third of what I bring in.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R13 800 this month. Last month it was closer to R17 000. I never know which one I'm getting until it's over.

slides.title: I stopped guessing between good months and bad ones
slides.body:
I upload my banking app statement to Beyond Horizon every month now, even the thin ones.

Seeing the stock spend against the quiet weeks finally made sense of why some months feel impossible.

No bank login needed.
